Core pipeline

spatial_proteomics.core.main()[source]

Run SpPrAn from the command-line interface.

Notes

This is the console entry point used by the sppran command. Validation or analysis errors are written to standard error and terminate the process with a non-zero exit code.

spatial_proteomics.core.spatial_proteomics_pipeline(config_path)[source]

Run the complete SpPrAn pipeline from a YAML configuration file.

Parameters:

config_path (str or pathlib.Path) – Path to the SpPrAn YAML configuration file.

Returns:

Analysis outputs are written to the output directory specified in the configuration file.

Return type:

None

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError – If the configuration file or required workspace directories do not exist.

  • spatial_proteomics.configuration.ConfigValidationError – If one or more configuration settings are invalid.

Notes

The configuration is validated before any spatial proteomics analysis is performed.

spatial_proteomics.core.sppran_steps(config)[source]

Run the main SpPrAn analysis steps from a validated configuration.

Parameters:

config (dict) – Validated SpPrAn configuration dictionary. The configuration must contain workspace settings, plotting options, cell-type definitions, colors, and output-control settings as produced by spatial_proteomics.configuration.load_config().

Returns:

Results are written to the configured output directory.

Return type:

None

Notes

After AnnData objects are created or loaded, execution is dispatched according to config["type_of_analysis"]:

  • "supervised" runs the rule-defined subtype workflow.

  • "unsupervised" runs exploratory marker-pattern discovery.

  • "full" performs exploratory discovery and then runs the supervised

workflow using discovered phenotypes as subtype definitions.

Configuration

Configuration loading and validation utilities for SpPrAn.

This module is responsible for:

  1. Safely parsing YAML configuration files.

  2. Rejecting duplicate YAML mapping keys.

  3. Applying configuration defaults.

  4. Validating configuration structure and cross-field rules.

  5. Converting workspace paths to pathlib.Path objects.

  6. Verifying that user-defined input and output directories exist.

The public entry point is load_config().

exception spatial_proteomics.configuration.ConfigValidationError(errors: list[str])[source]

Bases: ValueError

Report one or more invalid SpPrAn configuration settings.

Parameters:

errors (list of str) – Human-readable validation messages collected while checking the YAML configuration.

errors

Individual configuration errors.

Type:

list of str

spatial_proteomics.configuration.load_config(config_path: str | Path) → dict[source]

Load, validate, and normalize a SPPRAN YAML configuration file.

The function performs four steps:

  1. Validate the configuration-file path.

  2. Parse YAML safely while rejecting duplicate keys.

  3. Validate and normalize the configuration schema.

  4. Convert workspace paths to Path objects and verify that the user-defined input and output directories exist.

Relative input_dir and output_dir values are resolved relative to the YAML file’s directory.

Parameters:

config_path (str | Path) – Path to the YAML configuration file.

Returns:

Validated and normalized configuration dictionary. The returned workspace.input_dir and workspace.output_dir values are absolute Path objects.

Return type:

dict

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError – If the configuration file, input directory, or output directory does not exist.

  • IsADirectoryError – If config_path points to a directory instead of a file.

  • NotADirectoryError – If input_dir or output_dir exists but is not a directory.

  • ConfigValidationError – If the YAML is syntactically valid but contains invalid settings.

  • ValueError – If the YAML file cannot be parsed.

Notes

Configurations from before v0.3.0 that omit type_of_analysis are normalized to "supervised" for backward compatibility.

AnnData processing

spatial_proteomics.anndata.assign_cell_types_vectorized(data, cell_type_dict, container)[source]

Assign marker-defined phenotype labels to cells using vectorized comparisons.

Parameters:

  • data (pandas.DataFrame) – Cell-level table containing the positivity columns referenced by the phenotype rules.

  • cell_type_dict (dict) – Mapping from phenotype names to marker-state rules.

  • container (str) – Name of the parent population being subdivided. Use "General" for primary cell typing.

Returns:

Phenotype label for every row in data.

Return type:

pandas.Series

Notes

Cells are assigned in dictionary iteration order and only previously unassigned cells are evaluated for subsequent phenotypes. Cells not matching any rule are labeled "Other cells" at the general level.

spatial_proteomics.anndata.cleaned_data(file_names, output_dir, protein_markers, cell_subtype_dict, thresholds_file_names=None, filetype='tsv')[source]

Clean object-level spatial proteomics tables and create AnnData objects.

Parameters:

  • file_names (list of pathlib.Path) – Object-level input files to process.

  • output_dir (pathlib.Path) – Directory where SpPrAn result metadata will be written.

  • protein_markers (list of str) – Primary positivity-column names used for cell-type classification.

  • cell_subtype_dict (dict) – Hierarchical subtype definitions. Subtype marker columns are retained when required for downstream classification.

  • thresholds_file_names (list of pathlib.Path | "None" value for compatibility in previous iterations) – Object-level threshold files to process.

  • filetype ({"tsv", "csv"}, default="tsv") – Input table format.

Returns:

  • data_dicts (dict of str to pandas.DataFrame) – Cleaned per-sample tables used for phenotype assignment.

  • adata_dicts (dict of str to anndata.AnnData) – Per-sample AnnData objects containing cell-level measurements and spatial information.

Notes

When the DAPI positivity column is available, rows lacking nuclear DAPI positivity are removed. SpPrAn also records sample identifiers and the detected positivity-column names in the output directory.

The resulting AnnData objects represent individual segmented cells, not aggregated tissue regions.

spatial_proteomics.anndata.sets_and_subsets_cell_types(cell_type_dict, sub_cell_type_dict, protein_markers, output_dir, custom_colors, arrows_orientation='contains', type_of_analysis='supervised')[source]

Determine hierarchical subset relationships among marker-defined phenotypes.

Parameters:

  • cell_type_dict (dict) – Primary marker-based cell-type definitions.

  • sub_cell_type_dict (dict) – User-defined hierarchical subtype definitions.

  • protein_markers (list of str) – Primary marker names.

  • output_dir (pathlib.Path) – Output directory used for hierarchy visualizations and related files.

  • custom_colors (dict of str to str) – Hexadecimal color assigned to each phenotype.

  • arrows_orientation ({"contains", "isContained"}, default="contains") – Direction used to display relationships in hierarchy diagrams.

  • type_of_analysis ({"supervised", "unsupervised", "full"}, default="supervised") – Active analysis mode. The user-defined hierarchy figure is generated only for the supervised workflow at this stage.

Returns:

  • final_subsets (dict) – Final subset relationships for each hierarchy level.

  • subtype_definitions (dict) – Marker definitions associated with resolved phenotype subsets.

  • larger_groups (dict) – Parent or less-specific phenotype groups identified during hierarchy resolution.

  • custom_colors (dict) – Color mapping including any colors generated for intersecting phenotypes.

Notes

Cell populations are compared as sets defined by marker positivity rules. These subset relationships describe the logical phenotype definitions used by SpPrAn and should not automatically be interpreted as developmental lineage relationships.

Exploratory marker-defined phenotype analysis for SpPrAn.

This module identifies observed binary protein marker patterns within selected major cell populations, calculates phenotype abundance, stores phenotype labels and marker definitions in AnnData objects, and optionally compares phenotype abundance between two user-defined sample groups.

The workflow enumerates observed marker patterns rather than performing latent-space clustering.

spatial_proteomics.phenotype_analysis.unsupervised_phenotype_exploration_analysis(adata_dicts, adata_dir, exploratory_protein_markers, exploratory_protein_markers_short_name, cell_types_to_explore, cell_types_to_explore_short_name, dict_ctrl, dict_trtmnt, output_dir, overwrite_existing_files)[source]

Discover and quantify observed protein marker-defined phenotypes.

Parameters:

  • adata_dicts (dict of str to anndata.AnnData) – Samples containing major cell-type annotations and binary positivity data.

  • adata_dir (pathlib.Path) – Directory used to save updated AnnData objects.

  • exploratory_protein_markers (list of str) – Positivity protein markers selected for phenotype discovery.

  • exploratory_protein_markers_short_name (list of str) – Short names corresponding to the exploratory protein markers.

  • cell_types_to_explore (list of str) – Major cell populations in which phenotypes are quantified.

  • cell_types_to_explore_short_name (list of str) – Short names corresponding to the selected parent populations.

  • dict_ctrl (dict or None) – Optional filename-to-group mappings. Both are required for group comparison.

  • dict_trtmnt (dict or None) – Optional filename-to-group mappings. Both are required for group comparison.

  • output_dir (pathlib.Path) – SpPrAn output directory.

  • overwrite_existing_files (bool) – Whether existing outputs may be replaced.

Returns:

Updated AnnData objects containing discovered phenotype labels and protein marker-pattern mappings.

Return type:

dict of str to anndata.AnnData

Notes

Phenotypes correspond to observed binary positivity combinations rather than clusters. When two groups are supplied, common phenotype proportions are statistically compared and group-specific phenotypes are reported.

spatial_proteomics.intensity_analysis.plot_spatial_protein_marker_intensities(adata_dicts, output_dir, cmap='viridis', point_size=1, dpi=150)[source]

Plot spatial protein-marker intensity for every sample and protein marker.

Parameters:

  • adata_dicts (dict of str to anndata.AnnData) – Samples containing spatial coordinates in obsm["spatial"] and protein-marker intensities in X.

  • output_dir (pathlib.Path) – SpPrAn output directory.

  • cmap (str, default="viridis") – Matplotlib colormap used for intensity values.

  • point_size (float, default=1) – Scatter-point size for individual cells.

  • dpi (int or float, default=150) – Output image resolution.

Returns:

One PNG per sample and protein marker is written under plots/Spatial protein markers intensity plots.

Return type:

None

Notes

Each plot colors individual segmented cells by continuous protein-marker intensity, analogous to displaying gene expression on a single-cell embedding but retaining the cells’ actual tissue coordinates.

The current implementation scales each sample/protein marker independently using its observed minimum and maximum intensity. Consequently, colors should not be compared quantitatively between different sample panels unless a common scale is introduced.

Neighborhood analysis

Fixed-radius spatial neighborhood analyses for SpPrAn.

This module constructs spatial-neighbor graphs from single-cell coordinates and summarizes relationships among major marker-defined cell populations using Squidpy neighborhood enrichment, interaction matrices, and co-occurrence analysis.

Neighborhoods are defined geometrically from a user-specified physical/image radius rather than from PCA or expression-space nearest neighbors.

spatial_proteomics.neighborhoods.neighborhood_by_fixed_distance(adata_dicts, output_dir, dpi, save_anndata, overwrite_existing_files, neighborhood_radius_size=50, pixel_conversion_rate=1, max_distance_coocurrence=None)[source]

Run fixed-radius neighborhood analysis for all samples.

Parameters:

  • adata_dicts (dict of str to anndata.AnnData) – Per-sample annotated single-cell spatial proteomics data.

  • output_dir (pathlib.Path) – SpPrAn output directory.

  • dpi (int or float) – Resolution of exported neighborhood plots.

  • save_anndata (bool) – Whether AnnData objects containing neighborhood results should be saved.

  • overwrite_existing_files (bool) – Whether existing plot files may be replaced.

  • neighborhood_radius_size (float, default=50) – User-facing neighborhood radius.

  • pixel_conversion_rate (float, default=1) – Conversion factor between the user-facing radius unit and the spatial coordinate unit stored in AnnData.

  • max_distance_coocurrence (float or None, default=None) – Optional maximum distance shown in co-occurrence plots.

Returns:

AnnData objects containing the computed spatial-neighbor graph and Squidpy neighborhood-analysis results.

Return type:

dict of str to anndata.AnnData

Notes

The radius supplied to Squidpy is calculated as neighborhood_radius_size / pixel_conversion_rate.

This analysis defines neighborhoods from tissue/image coordinates. It does not require PCA, UMAP, or expression-space nearest-neighbor construction.

Advanced phenotype classification

Intensity-aware characterization of discovered SpPrAn phenotypes.

After unsupervised marker-pattern discovery, this module further stratifies positive-marker intensities within each sample into low, medium, and high categories. Thresholds are calculated from the distribution of positive cells for each marker using the 25th and 75th percentiles.

This analysis adds expression-strength information to existing discovered phenotypes; it does not redefine the original positivity-based phenotype.

spatial_proteomics.advanced_cell_classification.phenotype_advanced_cell_classification(adata_dicts, ct_short_names, epm_list, epm_short_names, output_dir, save_anndata, overwrite_existing_files)[source]

Run intensity-aware phenotype characterization across all samples.

Parameters:

  • adata_dicts (dict of str to anndata.AnnData) – Samples containing discovered phenotype assignments and marker positivity/intensity data.

  • ct_short_names (list of str) – Short names of parent cell populations explored in unsupervised mode.

  • epm_list (list of str) – Exploratory positivity-protein-marker names.

  • epm_short_names (list of str) – Short names corresponding positionally to epm_list.

  • output_dir (pathlib.Path) – SpPrAn output directory.

  • save_anndata (bool) – Whether classified AnnData objects should be written to disk.

  • overwrite_existing_files (bool) – Whether existing aggregate CSV outputs may be replaced.

Returns:

Updated AnnData objects containing per-cell protein-marker-intensity classes and per-protein-marker threshold metadata.

Return type:

dict of str to anndata.AnnData

Notes

Three aggregate CSV files are produced:

  • Protein marker intensity summary.csv;

  • Intensity profiles analysis.csv; and

  • Phenotype intensity summary.csv.

Intensity classes are sample-relative. They should be interpreted as within-sample expression-strength categories, not as standardized absolute expression levels across specimens.

  • order_dicc (dict) – Phenotype ordering grouped by rule specificity.

  • custom_colors (dict of str to str) – Phenotype color mapping.

Returns:

  • final_subsets (dict) – Resolved subset relationships.

  • subtype_definitions (dict) – Phenotype definitions generated during subset resolution.

  • larger_groups (list or dict) – Less-specific parent groups retained by the hierarchy.

  • custom_colors (dict) – Updated phenotype color mapping.

Notes

The directed graph represents logical set containment among marker-defined phenotypes rather than a biological developmental lineage.

spatial_proteomics.utils.plot_general_cell_hierarchy(protein_markers, cell_types, cell_sub_types, custom_colors, save_path, arrows_orientation='contains')[source]

Returns:

None

Notes

Nodes represent marker-defined populations. Parent-child edges describe nested phenotype definitions supplied by the user.
